name: Inca/Quechua (Cusco ethnic core)
notes: "Inca" (Sapa Inca) properly denoted the ruler, or the ruling ethnic elite of Cusco, not the empire or its multiethnic subject population, most of whom spoke Quechua and other languages and belonged to many distinct incorporated ethnic groups; the empire’s own name for itself was Tawantinsuyu ("the four regions/parts together"). Archaeologically continuous with the Killke culture of the Cusco basin (c. 900–1200 CE) — Killke pottery is found directly beneath Inca layers, and the Qoricancha site (later the empire’s central Inti temple) was already sacred under Killke occupation before the Inca imperial state existed. See pty_tawantinsuyu for the imperial polity.
